title: Org owner adds a payment method via Stripe-hosted Checkout (setup mode), then the checkout.session.completed webhook records it
description: There is no embedded Stripe Elements/card form anywhere in the client — 'add card' is a full-page redirect to a Stripe Checkout Session created in mode:'setup'. Verifies the real end-to-end path, not a fabricated in-app card form.
preconditions: Org has no stripeCustomerId yet; plan.status='pending_payment'
steps: Navigate to /billing-plans Overview tab and confirm the 'Set up payment' CTA is shown
Click the CTA, which calls billingService.startCheckoutSetup() -> POST /billing/v1/billing/checkout-session
Follow the redirect to the returned Stripe session.url and complete card entry on the Stripe-hosted page
Confirm Stripe redirects back to {CLIENT_APP_URL}/billing?setup=success
Wait for the checkout.session.completed webhook to be processed
expectedResult: Org's billing.stripeCustomerId is now set, the 'Set up payment' CTA no longer appears on Overview, and any frameworks previously pending payment are activated.

title: Selecting a higher tier on the Plans tab upgrades the plan and updates Overview without a full page reload
preconditions: Org on 'growth' tier with a payment method already on file
steps: Navigate to /billing-plans, open the Plans tab
Select the 'scale' plan and confirm via UpgradeModal
Observe the POST /billing/v1/billing/plan/upgrade call and its 200 response
Switch to the Overview tab without reloading the browser
expectedResult: Overview now shows tier 'scale', updated moduleConfig limits/usage bars, and no 'requires_contact' prompt since this tier is self-serve.

title: Downgrade is scheduled for the next renewal date, plan access is unchanged until then, and the scheduled change can be cancelled
description: Downgrades are never immediate — they are stored as a pending-tier-change applied at renewsAt. PendingDowngradeBanner surfaces the scheduled date and a Cancel action.
preconditions: Org on 'scale' tier, usage within 'growth' tier limits
steps: On the Plans tab, choose to downgrade to 'growth'
Confirm via DowngradeModal (no over-cap dialog expected since usage is within limits)
Reload /billing-plans and check the Overview tab for PendingDowngradeBanner
Verify a scale-tier-only feature (behind TierGate) is still fully accessible, not degraded
Click 'Cancel' on PendingDowngradeBanner
expectedResult: Banner reads 'scheduled to downgrade to growth on <renewsAt date>'. Scale-tier features remain accessible while the downgrade is pending. After clicking Cancel, DELETE /billing/v1/billing/plan/pending-change succeeds and the banner disappears with the org remaining on 'scale' tier indefinitely.

title: A TierGate-wrapped premium feature shows the upgrade alert on a lower tier and unlocks after a real upgrade
description: TierGate.jsx is documented as cosmetic-only and 'fails open' if entitlements haven't resolved; real enforcement is the backend requireFeature middleware. This case verifies the two actually agree end-to-end, since a UI-only gate with no backend check would be a security gap.
preconditions: Org on 'growth' tier, which lacks feature 'vciso.advisor'
steps: Navigate to a vCISO page/section gated behind TierGate for 'vciso.advisor'
Observe the Alert: '<Feature> feature — This feature requires the <tier> plan or above.' with an 'Upgrade plan' button
Attempt to call the underlying API route directly (bypassing the UI) while still on 'growth' tier
Upgrade the org to a tier that includes 'vciso.advisor', then revisit the same page
expectedResult: Direct API call is rejected 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE even though the button is merely hidden client-side (confirms server-side parity, not just a UI label). After the real upgrade, the page renders the actual feature content instead of the gate alert.

title: Invoice history lists Stripe invoices with correctly formatted amount/date, and PDF is obtained via Stripe's hosted invoice page
description: There is no backend PDF proxy/download endpoint — the app only stores and links to Stripe's hosted_invoice_url, which itself offers a PDF download on Stripe's own page.
preconditions: Org has at least 2 historical Stripe invoices with different amounts and currencies formatting
steps: Navigate to the invoice history page (/billing/invoices)
Verify each row's amount matches the Stripe invoice's amount_due, formatted as currency
Verify issuedAt is formatted as a readable date, not a raw epoch/ISO string
Click a row to open its hostedInvoiceUrl
On the Stripe-hosted page, download the PDF
expectedResult: Amounts and dates render correctly and match the Stripe dashboard for the same invoices. The PDF download happens entirely on Stripe's hosted page; there is no in-app 'Download PDF' button that produces a locally-generated file.

title: Full-account cancellation (customer.subscription.deleted) revokes access immediately with no grace period
description: Unlike framework-level cancellation, a whole-org Stripe subscription deletion sets Organization.subscription.status and SubscriptionOrg.status to 'cancelled' immediately — there is no org-level grace window.
preconditions: Org has an active org-level Stripe subscription
steps: Cancel the org's Stripe subscription (via Stripe dashboard/test mode) so a customer.subscription.deleted event fires
Wait for the webhook to be processed
Log in as an org user and attempt to access any paid-tier feature
expectedResult: Both Organization.subscription.status and SubscriptionOrg.status read 'cancelled' immediately after the webhook, and paid-tier features are inaccessible with no grace period grant.

title: Cancelling a single framework's subscription enters a 90-day grace period and revokes the framework license immediately
description: Framework-scoped cancellation is handled differently from full-account cancellation: frameworkSubscriptions.$.status becomes 'grace' with graceEndsAt = now + 90 days, while ClientFramework.status is set to 'license_revoked' right away — i.e. the license is revoked immediately even though billing calls it a 'grace period'. Worth confirming this naming doesn't mislead users into thinking they retain framework access during the 90 days.
preconditions: Org has 2+ frameworks each with their own framework-level Stripe subscription
steps: Cancel only one framework's Stripe subscription so a framework-scoped customer.subscription.deleted event fires
Wait for the webhook to be processed
Check the framework's subscription status and graceEndsAt, and the ClientFramework.status
As an org user, attempt to access that framework's compliance map
expectedResult: frameworkSubscriptions status='grace' with graceEndsAt ~90 days out, but ClientFramework.status='license_revoked' immediately, and the framework's compliance map/features are inaccessible right away (grace period does not extend feature access, only likely data-retention/reactivation window).

title: Overview tab's 'Renews In N Days' stat is the only renewal/trial countdown surfaced — there is no dedicated trial-ending banner
description: No trial countdown banner component exists anywhere in vibrantix-client-panel. The closest analog is BillingOverview.jsx's generic 'Renews In N Days' stat card computed from plan.renewsAt, shown for any plan status, not specifically flagged during a trial or when trial-ending is imminent.
preconditions: Org is on a 'trial' status plan with trialExpiresAt 2 days out
steps: Navigate to /billing-plans Overview tab
Locate the 'Renews In N Days' stat card
Confirm no separate persistent trial-ending warning banner is present anywhere in the app shell (top nav, dashboard, or billing pages)
expectedResult: Current behavior: only the generic 'Renews In N Days' stat reflects the approaching trialExpiresAt; there is no visually distinct 'trial ending soon' banner or in-app countdown beyond this stat card. Document as a gap versus the commonly expected trial-countdown-banner UX rather than a defect against a feature that was implemented differently.
